title: test(fields): pin openNativePicker's click path through DateField (objectui#7570)
body:
Fixes #7570

## What this closes

`packages/fields/src/widgets/openNativePicker.ts` was named by **zero** test files in the repo. `DateField` is its **sole** router — the `onClick` handler is the only call site — and none of `DateField`'s existing cases fires a click, so that line had never been executed by the suite. "This file is well covered" was true of the file and false of the line.

This is a **coverage-gap** card, not a bug report. The filer explicitly did not claim a live defect, and **no behaviour changed**: `openNativePicker.ts` and `DateField.tsx` are byte-identical to `origin/main` on this branch (`git diff origin/main -- packages/fields/src/widgets/openNativePicker.ts packages/fields/src/widgets/DateField.tsx` is empty).

The card's own instrument now answers, and its control is unchanged:

```
$ git grep -l 'openNativePicker' -- '*.test.ts' '*.test.tsx'
packages/fields/src/widgets/openNativePicker.test.tsx        # was: no output
```

## The pins

One new file, `packages/fields/src/widgets/openNativePicker.test.tsx` — 8 tests, no other source touched.

| # | pin |
|---|-----|
| PIN 1 | clicking the field invokes the helper **on the field's own input** (the receiver of the `showPicker` call is asserted, so handing the helper some other element fails) |
| PIN 2 | a host-supplied `onClick` arriving through DOM props is **not swallowed** |
| PIN 3 | one click runs **both** — neither statement short-circuits the other |

Plus five direct tests of the helper itself, which is where the "zero coverage" in the card's title actually is: an enabled input opens the picker; `disabled` and `readOnly` stay shut; a throwing `showPicker` is swallowed; an absent `showPicker` is a no-op.

### Why the helper is NOT mocked

Mocking `openNativePicker` would let these tests assert that we called the thing we mocked — coverage up, protection zero. The real helper runs, and the observable side effect is `showPicker`, spied on the prototype.

That stand-in is load-bearing rather than decoration: happy-dom 20.11.2 does **not** implement `HTMLInputElement.showPicker`, and the helper's call is optional (`input.showPicker?.()`), so without a stand-in the click produces no observable effect at all and every assertion here would pass for an empty reason. This is the same route the form renderer's copy of the behaviour already takes (`packages/components/src/renderers/form/__tests__/form-date-picker-click.test.tsx`). What is pinned is the **call path**; the browser's own picker behaviour is out of reach of this DOM and is deliberately not claimed.

### What is deliberately NOT pinned

The **order** of the two statements in the handler. Swapping them changes no observable outcome, so an order assertion would fail a legitimate refactor while guarding nothing. PIN 3 pins the thing a short-circuit actually breaks: a single click runs both.

## Ablation — each pin is shown to fail when its code is deleted

A coverage test that stays green when the code under test is deleted is the exact counterfeit this card exists to prevent, so every pin was ablated.

| leg | line deleted | file | result |
|---|---|---|---|
| A | `openNativePicker(e.currentTarget);` | `DateField.tsx` | exit 1 — **2 failed / 6 passed**, naming PIN 1 and PIN 3 |
| B | `domProps.onClick?.(e);` | `DateField.tsx` | exit 1 — **2 failed / 6 passed**, naming PIN 2 and PIN 3 |
| C | `if (input.disabled or input.readOnly) return;` (the guard, spelled with the real operator in the file) | `openNativePicker.ts` | exit 1 — **2 failed / 6 passed**, naming "stays shut for a disabled input" and "stays shut for a readOnly input" |

Vitest named the failures itself, e.g. for leg A:

```
FAIL |dom| packages/fields/src/widgets/openNativePicker.test.tsx > DateField — the sole router into openNativePicker (objectui#7570) > PIN 1: clicking the field invokes the helper on the field's own input
FAIL |dom| packages/fields/src/widgets/openNativePicker.test.tsx > DateField — the sole router into openNativePicker (objectui#7570) > PIN 3: one click runs BOTH — neither statement short-circuits the other
Test Files  1 failed (1)
     Tests  2 failed | 6 passed (8)
```

Discipline each leg followed, so the readings are about the tree they claim to be about:

- **The mutation was proven on disk BEFORE the run** — `git hash-object` moved (leg A: `8a472aed2` to `5a499721a`) and the anchor count flipped `1` to `0`. A zero-hit edit exits 0 and reads like a successful ablation, so the harness refuses to run the leg unless both observations flip.
- **Restoration was proven BY STATE, not by assuming the trap fired** — `git checkout HEAD -- ABSOLUTE_PATH` (never the bare form, which restores *from the index* and would put the mutation back), then `git diff HEAD` empty **and** `hash-object` equal to the HEAD blob. An empty hash is read as failure, not as "nothing to compare".
- **A `trap ... EXIT INT TERM` with absolute paths** covered the crash path, and the implementation was committed *before* the first mutation, so `HEAD` genuinely holds it.
- **No build/`dist` leg is involved.** The test imports both mutated files by **relative path**, so Vitest transforms the source on disk and there is no `dist/` in the resolution path that a stale artifact could hide behind.

## Verification

All runs from the repo root, on the final commit `0a9ef8e1b`; exit codes captured by redirecting first, never through a pipe.

| command | result |
|---|---|
| `pnpm exec vitest run packages/fields/src/widgets/openNativePicker.test.tsx` | 1 file, **8 passed** |
| `pnpm exec vitest run packages/fields/` (whole package, after restore) | **134 files, 2186 tests, all passed** |
| `pnpm exec turbo run type-check --filter @object-ui/fields` | **11 tasks successful** |
| `pnpm exec eslint packages/fields/src/widgets/openNativePicker.test.tsx` | exit 0, no findings |
| `node scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs` | see below |

The type-check program really contains the new file — `tsc -p tsconfig.test.json --listFiles` names `packages/fields/src/widgets/openNativePicker.test.tsx`, so "type-check is clean" is a statement about it and not around it.

### Changeset

A test-only change under a released package's `src/` still owes a declaration. The **empty-frontmatter** form is the first-class passing shape for "this releases nothing":

BEFORE (`exit 1`):

```
❌  1 source file(s) of 1 released package(s) changed, and this change adds no changeset:
      @object-ui/fields
          packages/fields/src/widgets/openNativePicker.test.tsx
```

AFTER (`exit 0`), with `.changeset/opennativepicker-coverage-7570.md` added:

```
✅  1 source file(s) of 1 released package(s) changed, and this change declares 1 changeset(s): .changeset/opennativepicker-coverage-7570.md.
    Every one of them has an EMPTY frontmatter — declared as releasing nothing, which
    is the explicit exemption and a complete answer to this gate.
```

`node scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs` also passes (`✅  No changeset declares a major bump.`).

### Not run, stated plainly

The repo-wide `pnpm lint` and `pnpm test` farms, and the rest of the `check:*` family — CI runs them exactly once on this PR. Lint was narrowed to the one changed file; tests were run at the file level and then at the whole-package level.
